injectivityByExhibitedInverse.claim: the encoding of every record type in this artifact is INJECTIVE, so two distinct logical values cannot produce one preimage.
injectivityByExhibitedInverse.proofForm: NOT by inspection and NOT by enumerating collision cases. A TOTAL DECODER is exhibited: for each record type it reads the record tag, then for each declared field in declared order reads uint8(tag), uint32be(len) and exactly len bytes, and RAISES on a tag mismatch, a tag in the wrong order, a length that overruns the buffer, a missing field, a field present that the variant forbids, or any trailing byte. decode(encode(x)) == x for every x in the accepted domain, so encode has a left inverse, so encode is injective, so H(encode(x)) collides only if SHA-256 does.
injectivityByExhibitedInverse.whatBecomesINEXPRESSIBLE: the concatenation ambiguity where ('ab','c') and ('a','bc') share a preimage. It is not a case to be listed and guarded; it has no representation, because every component carries its own explicit length before its bytes, so the field boundary set is a function of the byte string alone.
injectivityByExhibitedInverse.theVariantCase: PolicyDerivationInputV1 exists in two variants. They cannot share a preimage because field 0x81 carries the variant text in a length-framed component at a fixed ordinal, and because the incomplete variant carries a tenth field (0x8F) the completed variant forbids. Vectors PDD-1 and PDD-6 encode the SAME stageInput, rules, policy, findings and exactCoverage under the two variants and publish two distinct digests. Vectors REJ-10 and REJ-11 show both encoders refuse a completed record carrying deficiency and an incomplete record missing it.
injectivityByExhibitedInverse.executed: the decoder was RUN against every record encoded for every vector in this artifact and the round trip was asserted each time. Totality was separately attacked: truncation, an appended byte and a swapped record tag all raise (see testVectors.decoderTotality). This is not a claim about a decoder that was never run.
injectivityByExhibitedInverse.domainOfInjectivity: records. Both recipes commit a SINGLETON set, so the set-commitment layer's deliberate permutation-insensitivity is not reached by either published identity. It IS reached one level down, inside CapabilityManifestV1's providers, relations, platformIds, coverageForAbsent and relationIds lists, which ARE sets and ARE order-insensitive by design: vector CAP-REV reverses the full profile's providers[] and gets the SAME id. That is the intended property of a capability manifest identity and it is stated here so a reviewer can reject it if it is not.

A conforming implementation must reject a boolean, a float or a numeric string where an integer is declared, and a non-string where text is declared, BEFORE it computes anything here. whatIsCommittedTo.answer: THE DERIVATION, NOT THE OUTCOME. The record commits to everything the policy evaluation consumed and to nothing it produced as its verdict.
whatIsCommittedTo.soTheVERDICTIsEXCLUDED: deliberately. If the verdict were inside, derivationDigest would be an outcome digest -- redundant with the sibling 'verdict' field it sits beside, and unable to answer the one question the field exists for: given the same inputs, did two runs derive their verdicts from the same thing. With the verdict outside, a verifier that recomputes derivationDigest and finds a match, beside two different verdicts, has MECHANICALLY DETECTED a non-deterministic policy engine. That is the property the field can carry and an outcome digest cannot.
whatIsCommittedTo.thisIsADESIGNDECISION: and it is the single most reviewable sentence in R-B. R-1's ten positive vectors cannot discriminate it. Measured: THREE vectors share the verdict 'indeterminate' -- R1V15-POS-04, -05 and -06 -- and they carry three DISTINCT derivationDigest constants (sha256:6666..., sha256:8888..., sha256:9999...). So the verdict alone plainly does not determine the field. But each of the three also differs from the others in exactCoverage and deficiency, so a recipe that INCLUDED the verdict would predict three distinct constants too. The vectors are consistent with both readings and settle neither. A reviewer who wants the verdict inside should say so; the recipe would change by one field frame.

Under this recipe the field is load-bearing rather than decorative.

strongestObjectionTheAuthorExpects.objection: THE DOMAIN SEPARATORS ARE INVENTED, AND SECTION 7.1 SAYS THE ONE THING NOBODY MAY DO IS INVENT. 'opensip.delivery.v1', 'capability-manifest-v1', 'opensip.r1-core.v1' and 'policy-derivation-v1' exist nowhere in this corpus before this file. Everything else here is transcription or arithmetic; those four strings are creation, and they are the load-bearing part -- a domain separator IS the identity's separation from every other identity. So the artifact's own account of itself ('proposes, does not invent') is at best a distinction of intent, and the freeze does not grade on intent.
strongestObjectionTheAuthorExpects.authorsAnswer: PARTIALLY CONCEDED, and the concession is recorded as declaredUnresolvedDependencies.DUD-1 rather than argued away. Three things are offered against it and none of them is a refutation. FIRST: a domain separator cannot be transcribed, because a separator that already exists belongs to another identity and reusing it is the exact failure it exists to prevent -- vectors XD-1 through XD-4 demonstrate that with digests. Any recipe for a new identity mints one string or has no separation; the alternative to minting is not transcribing, it is not having a recipe. SECOND: what is normally the hard part -- the framing, the field order, the scalar rules, the ordering, the injectivity argument -- is transcribed and was gated against evaluation-proof.v8's own goldens at 51 assertions before any new value was computed, and R-A's field ORDER is delivery.v2's own 'required' arrays in their own order while R-B's field SET is derived from R-1's closed API and four measured exclusions. The invention is confined to four strings and two tag bands. THIRD: section 7.1 forbids CLOSING these rows by record, blueprint, checker or implementer, and requires a BINDING ARTIFACT. A binding artifact has to contain these four strings too. The question a reviewer must actually settle is not whether the strings are new -- they must be -- but WHO IS ALLOWED TO WRITE THEM DOWN. If the answer is 'only DELIVERY, and only R-1', then this file is at most an input to those two surfaces and should be graded as one. THE AUTHOR CANNOT SETTLE THAT AND DOES NOT CLAIM TO.
